name: John Cutts, Lord Cutts
bio: John Cutts, Baron Cutts of Gowran (1661–1707), was an English soldier who served under William III and Marlborough, nicknamed “the Salamander” for his courage under fire.
He also wrote occasional verse, collected in his Poetical Exercises (1687).

poems.title: Song
poems.author: John Cutts, Lord Cutts
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of English Verse (1900)
poems.text:
Only tell her that I love:
  Leave the rest to her and Fate:
Some kind planet from above
May perhaps her pity move:
  Lovers on their stars must wait.--
Only tell her that I love!

Why, O why should I despair!
  Mercy’s pictured in her eye:
If she once vouchsafe to hear,
Welcome Hope and farewell Fear!
  She’s too good to let me die.--
Why, O why should I despair?
